request.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows, SUM(coalesced_count) AS events, MIN(timestamp) AS first_seen, MAX(timestamp) AS last_seen FROM query_logs

SELECT client_ip, CAST(timestamp AS DATE) as day, SUM(COALESCE(coalesced_count, 1)) as queries
FROM query_logs
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2

SELECT client_ip, query_name, SUM(COALESCE(coalesced_count, 1)) as cnt
FROM query_logs
WHERE query_name LIKE '%example.com%'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY cnt DESC
LIMIT 100

SELECT client_ip, strftime('%Y-%m', timestamp) as month, COUNT(DISTINCT query_name) as unique_domains
FROM query_logs
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2

SELECT client_ip, COUNT(DISTINCT query_name) as unique_domains, SUM(COALESCE(coalesced_count, 1)) as total
FROM query_logs
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY unique_domains DESC
LIMIT 20
SELECT SUM(sin(a.latency_microseconds*b.latency_microseconds)) FROM query_logs a CROSS JOIN query_logs b

raw_oracle_scope_correction.reason: Both archive arguments to verify-final-originals.sh refer to archives-stopped. The one-million-query run had already archived 983040 records before the first journal snapshot. A hash comparison to those same files is self-comparison, not archive-write integrity evidence. Stdout query lines omit raw fields and are not a complete original-payload witness.
